# Overview

The main analysis places `mean_loss` and `var_loss` in the community the three
dependency-MI indices form. That community is therefore defined partly by the
nodes whose membership is the finding, which makes the finding hard to read on
its own terms.

This run holds **both** predictability nodes out and asks what is left. If
`amod_mi`, `dobj_mi` and `advmod_mi` still group together, the community is a
property of the MI battery that predictability joins. If they scatter, the
community was held together by predictability, and the main result should be
described as predictability organising the MI indices rather than joining them.

The other two sensitivity runs hold out one node each:
`network-no-varloss.qmd` and `network-no-meanloss.qmd`.

```{r}
#| label: drop-parameter
#| code-fold: false

# Both predictability nodes held out: a 13-node battery with no focal node.
# The shared body switches every focal-dependent section over to the
# dependency-MI readout when `pred_vars` comes back empty.
drop_var <- c("mean_loss", "var_loss")
```
